facet_selection_reasoning: This combination targets two interrelated misconceptions: B15 (misinterpreting confidence level as probability of including the true mean for a specific interval) and B17 (thinking higher confidence yields a shorter, more precise interval). These are paired with A4 (correct interpretation of confidence level as a long-run frequency across replications) and A6 (understanding that higher confidence level leads to a wider interval). Together they form a coherent item around what 'confidence level' means and its directional effect on interval width. This specific combination has not been used before and differs meaningfully from Items 1, 2, and 5 which touched on some overlapping facets in different groupings.

item.stem:
A researcher calculates a 95% confidence interval and reports: "We are 95% confident that the true population mean lies within this interval." The researcher then decides to recalculate the interval using a 99% confidence level instead of 95%, keeping everything else the same.

For each of the following statements, indicate whether it is True or False.

options.text: The 99% confidence interval will be wider than the 95% confidence interval.
options.rationale: A higher confidence level requires a larger critical value (e.g., z* = 2.576 for 99% vs. 1.96 for 95%), which directly increases the margin of error and thus the width of the interval. This correctly reflects A6.

options.text: The 99% confidence interval will be narrower because a higher confidence level produces a more precise estimate.
options.rationale: This reflects the classic B17 misconception that higher confidence leads to a more precise (narrower) interval. In reality, increasing the confidence level increases interval width (A6), the opposite of what this statement claims.

options.text: There is a 99% probability that the true population mean lies within the newly calculated interval.
options.rationale: This statement misinterprets the confidence level as a probability that the true mean lies within one specific interval (B15). The correct interpretation (A4) is that 99% of all intervals constructed this way would capture the true mean across repeated sampling; any single interval either does or does not contain the mean.

options.text: If the researcher repeated the study many times and calculated a 99% confidence interval each time, about 99% of those intervals would contain the true population mean.
options.rationale: This correctly interprets the confidence level in terms of the long-run frequency of intervals capturing the true parameter across repeated replications, which is the proper interpretation of A4.

item.explanation: This item targets four facets. Option A (correct) and Option B (incorrect) together probe A6 and B17: a higher confidence level widens the interval because the critical value increases, contrary to the misconception that higher confidence yields a more precise, narrower estimate. Option C (incorrect) probes B15 and A4: interpreting the confidence level as the probability that one particular interval contains the true mean is a common error; the correct frequentist interpretation, demonstrated in Option D (correct), is that the stated percentage of all such intervals constructed over repeated sampling would capture the population parameter.

judge_report.item_stem_preview: A researcher calculates a 95% confidence interval and reports: 'We are 95% confident that the true population mean lies within this interval.' The researcher then decides to recalculate the interval using a 99% confidence level instead of 95%, keeping everything else the same.

option_assessments.reasoning: This statement correctly describes the relationship between the confidence level and the width of the interval, which perfectly aligns with goal facet A6.

The statement explicitly embodies misconception B17 (higher confidence leads to a more precise/narrower interval). While it is the logical opposite of A6, tagging it primarily with the targeted misconception (B17) is the standard psychometric practice.

This statement explicitly reflects misconception B15, interpreting the confidence interval as a probability of containing the true mean. Although it violates goal facet A4, B15 alone is the most precise tag.
The statement provides the correct frequentist interpretation of a confidence interval across repeated sampling, perfectly matching goal facet A4.
